close_reason: handle_get now batch-serializes the entire list via serialize_value(&list). One serializer construction instead of N for the Vec<O> case. Wire shape unchanged. handle_query_changes added_items_json builder needs per-element {id, index} construction so cannot trivially batch — out of scope.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/handlers.rs:114-117 — handle_get serializes the returned objects with:

  let list_json: Vec<Value> = list
      .iter()
      .map(serialize_value)
      .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;

For each object the helper calls serde_json::to_value, which constructs and discards an intermediate Serializer per call. For a Mailbox/get over 10k mailboxes, this is 10k separate to_value invocations.

A single serde_json::to_value(&list) over the entire Vec<O> would amortize the serializer construction. Or build the response directly with serde_json::Value::Array and let the json! macro slot it in.

Marginal at small N. Worth flagging for Mailbox/get and Email/get on large accounts (~100k+ objects). The current pattern also obscures the per-object error: if object #5000 fails to serialize, the error includes no positional info. Batch-serialization would either succeed for the whole list or fail with a structured serde_json error.

Fix: replace with `let list_json = serde_json::to_value(&list).map_err(|e| JmapError::server_fail(e.to_string()))?;` — one alloc, identical wire shape.

(The same pattern in handle_query_changes added_items_json builder at handlers.rs:347-357 has the same flavor but is inherent to the AddedItem-to-Value shape transform — those need {id, index} keys constructed, so batch is harder.)
title: handle_get serializes objects one-by-one rather than batch-serializing
